macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major crypto assets rebound as U.S.-Iran tensions ease
items.summary: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Dogecoin rose late Sunday after markets interpreted a pause in U.S.-Iran hostilities as reducing immediate geopolitical risk. Related reports said BTC recovered around the $63,000 area after a prior slide under $61,500, with traders pointing to a potential short-term bottom.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly drops below $65,000 amid renewed volatility
items.summary: The Verge reported Bitcoin falling below $65,000, reflecting continued price swings in the crypto market. The move comes amid broader uncertainty tied to macro and geopolitical developments.

items.title: Google tightens Chrome Web Store rules on prediction market extensions
items.summary: Google updated its Chrome Web Store Developer Program Policies to prohibit extensions that facilitate real-money prediction market transactions, with the change set to take effect on Aug. 1, 2026. The policy shift is relevant to crypto-linked prediction market activity.

items.title: EU reportedly preparing to reopen MiCA rulebook for non-EU stablecoin issuers
items.summary: EU diplomats told Euronews that the European Union is considering reopening parts of its Markets in Crypto-Assets framework, likely in 2027, to address non-EU stablecoin issuers. This would be one of the most significant upcoming regulatory developments for crypto in Europe.

items.title: SEC chief Atkins adds three crypto rulemaking initiatives to agenda
items.summary: A report in Drimble said SEC Chairman Atkins has placed three concrete crypto regulatory initiatives on the agency’s agenda. The item signals continued U.S. regulatory activity around digital assets and market structure.

items.title: SWIFT launches blockchain-ledger pilot with 17 banks
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that SWIFT has launched a blockchain ledger and is piloting tokenized deposits with 17 banks. The development is notable because it could expand blockchain-based settlement infrastructure in mainstream finance.

items.title: Tokenized stocks hit record levels as blockchain asset activity accelerates
items.summary: ChainCatcher cited data showing tokenized stocks soaring to a record $3.4 billion, with two networks leading the growth. The report points to accelerating interest in tokenized real-world assets and blockchain-based trading products.

items.title: Crypto thefts and hacks remain elevated in 2026
items.summary: ChainCatcher reported that Immunefi said hacking incidents in the crypto industry reached a new high in the first half of 2026, with losses of about $972 million. The figure underscores persistent security risks across DeFi and broader crypto infrastructure.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across applications and files, expanding its push into professional AI tools and workplace automation. The launch intensifies competition with Anthropic and other enterprise AI vendors.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, positioning it more directly against paid AI offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic. The move signals continued pressure to monetize frontier model access.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release points to faster, more natural conversational AI for assistants and voice-driven applications.

items.title: Grok 4.5 released for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model so far and targeting coding and agentic workflows. The release adds to the rapid pace of major model updates in the AI market.

items.title: Meta plans in-house AI chip manufacturing
items.summary: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an AI chip from September as it works to expand computing power to 14 gigawatts next year, according to an internal memo reviewed by Reuters. The effort reflects a broader industry shift toward custom silicon to reduce dependence on external suppliers.

items.title: Meta announces major Alberta data center buildout
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to support growing AI infrastructure needs. The project underscores the continuing industry race to secure compute capacity for model training and deployment.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move highlights continued emphasis on governance and safety oversight in frontier AI.

items.title: Micron commits more than $250 billion to U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging demand for memory chips in the AI era. The announcement reflects how AI demand is reshaping semiconductor capital spending.
